summary: The cardholder starts with no prior balance, makes purchases that push the account above the credit limit, and then reaches statement close while still over limit. The scenario is designed to probe over-limit behavior at statement close while also including the modeled minimum-payment and grace-period obligations in the timeline.
assumptions: The account begins a new billing cycle with no previous balance, so the purchase grace-period condition is satisfied for this cycle.

The issuer allows the purchase authorizations to post even though the resulting balance exceeds the disclosed credit limit; the contract says the cardholder promises not to exceed the limit and may still owe over-limit credit that is extended.
No payments are made before statement close, so the statement new balance remains above the credit limit.

A payment due date is set after statement close so the minimum payment obligation can be represented, but the archetype focuses on the over-limit condition at statement close rather than later delinquency outcomes.

The grace-period obligation is represented by the statement-close timing: statement close occurs 30 days after cycle start, which is at least 25 days after the first new purchases, so no purchase interest is imposed before that minimum grace window expires.
The minimum payment obligation is included with a due-check event referencing the modeled clause, but it is treated as unmet in this archetype because no payment is made by the due date.
